kaliganj-langcha.desc: Langcha is a fried, elongated sweet made from chhana and flour, cooked until dark brown and then dipped in syrup. In Kaliganj it is the sweet everyone names first, and the popular shops sell hundreds of kilograms a day. Inside it is soft and juicy, outside slightly firm. Buy early in the day.

gazi-kalu-champaboti.desc: The tale of Gazi Pir, his companion Kalu and Princess Champaboti is one of Bengal's best-known folk legends, and Barobazar is named as its setting. Wandering singers once performed it as Gazir gaan with painted scroll pictures called Gazir pat, showing Gazi riding a tiger. Mounds and ponds around Barobazar are pointed out as places in the story. The legend reflects the mix of Sufi and local beliefs in rural Bengal.
blocks: Good to know
Ask elders at Barobazar about the story; performances are rare now but sometimes staged at fairs.

glance: Weekly village haats around Kotchandpur and Kaliganj
jhenaidah-patali-gur.desc: Jhenaidah lies in the same date palm belt as Jashore, and winter villages smell of boiling sap. Tappers collect the juice before dawn, and families reduce it over fires into thick gur, pouring some into moulds to set as patali. It is eaten plain, crumbled over muri, or cooked into pitha. Fresh patali is softer and more fragrant than market stock.

glance: 190 km to Jhenaidah by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
dhol-samudra-dighi.desc: Dhol Samudra is a broad excavated pond on the outskirts of Jhenaidah town. Local tradition credits it to Raja Mukut Ray, a ruler of the area, and tells of drums beaten while it was dug. Today it is a quiet place of open water and tree-lined banks. Locals come for evening walks.
blocks: How to get there
A rickshaw or auto from Jhenaidah town.
Good to know
Late afternoon is the nicest time.

glance: 190 km to Jhenaidah by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
naldanga-rajbari.desc: The Naldanga estate in Kaliganj was founded around 1650 by Bishnudas Hazra, a former ascetic, and his descendants held it for about 300 years. They built around eight temples here, among them shrines to Kali, Lakshmi, Ganesh, Durga, Taramoni, Vishnu and Rajeshwari. Little remains of the palace itself, but the temples have been repaired several times and are in fairly good shape, their tall towers standing together beside the old estate grounds. It is one of the better-known day trips from Jhenaidah town.
blocks: How to get there
From Jhenaidah or Kaliganj take a bus or CNG towards Naldanga (roughly 18–20 km from Jhenaidah town), then a short van ride to the Rajbari.
Good to know
These are active temples; take off shoes where asked. Combine with the Mallikpur banyan tree and Barobazar in one Kaliganj day.

glance: 190 km to Jhenaidah by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
barobazar-mosques.desc: Barobazar in Kaliganj was an important town in the 15th and 16th centuries, and archaeologists have uncovered several brick mosques and large ponds here. Some, like the Galakata and Jor Bangla mosques, have been restored and are used for prayer again. The site has the feel of a ruined town absorbed back into rural life. Local legend connects Barobazar with Gazi Pir and his companions.
blocks: How to get there
Barobazar lies on the Jashore–Jhenaidah road; buses stop at the bazar, then explore by van or on foot.
Good to know
Hire a local van driver who knows the scattered sites; dress modestly at active mosques.

mallikpur-banyan-tree.desc: At Bethuli near Mallikpur in Kaliganj, a single banyan has sent down aerial roots for two or three centuries, each becoming a new trunk. The original tree has died, but its offspring still form a shady, connected grove often described locally as the largest banyan in Asia. Hindu devotees treat the site as sacred, and stories warn against cutting its branches. Walking beneath the canopy feels like entering a green hall.
blocks: How to get there
From Kaliganj town, take an auto or van about 8–10 km east to Bethuli village.
Good to know
Don't climb or break roots; the trees are under stress from visitors.

glance: 190 km to Jhenaidah by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
miyar-dalan.desc: Miyar Dalan stands at Muraridaha, about three kilometres from the centre of Jhenaidah town, on the north bank of the Nabaganga river. Building began in 1229 and ended in 1236 of the Bangla calendar (roughly 1822–1829). Over the main gate a verse is carved naming the village, a lady called Bibi Ashrafunnesa, and the cost of 75,000 taka. The zamindar sold the house around Partition, and some locals call it Selim Chowdhury's house after the buyer. It is badly decayed now, and a story of a tunnel running under the river adds to its air of mystery.
blocks: How to get there
A rickshaw or easy bike from Jhenaidah town to Muraridaha (about 3 km).
Good to know
The structure is unsafe in places; stay out of crumbling rooms. Late afternoon by the river is the nicest time.

glance: Molla Hotel, Hamdaha bus stand near Rezaul Filling Station, Jhenaidah town
molla-hotel-beef-bhuna.desc: Mridha Roshan Ali Molla opened Molla Hotel in Jhenaidah in 1968. The building was destroyed in the 1971 war; he started again in 1972 and moved to Hamdaha in 1984, and his son has run it since 1987. Its beef bhuna is what people travel for, with mutton bhuna a close second, eaten with rice or wheat roti. The hotel is open 24 hours with staff working in shifts, which makes it a reliable stop on the highway.

glance: 190 km to Jhenaidah by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
shailkupa-shahi-mosque.desc: The Shahi Mosque in Shailkupa is a protected monument from the pre-Mughal sultanate era. Its brick walls carry several small domes and corner turrets typical of the period. It still serves as a place of prayer for the town. The Kumar river flows close by, making a pleasant stroll after the visit.
blocks: How to get there
Buses from Jhenaidah to Shailkupa take about 40 minutes; the mosque is a short rickshaw ride from the bazar.
Good to know
Avoid prayer times and dress modestly.
